nonop.text: The Company recorded other expense of $(1,144,134) for the three months ended March 31, 2026, compared to other income of $4,351,668 for the three months ended March 31, 2025, representing an decrease in other expense of $5,495,802 or 126%. net.heading: Net Income (Loss)
net.text:
Net loss for the three months ended March 31, 2026 was $2,571,394, compared to Net Income of $189,176 for the three months ended March 31, 2025, , representing an increase in net loss of $2,760,570 or approximately 1,459%. The decrease in net loss was primarily due to a decrease in the change in fair value of contingent consideration of $4,260,000, a decrease in general and administrative expenses of $2,803,335 and a loss on the extinguishment of debt of $1,086,116.

Net loss for the nine months ended March 31, 2026, and 2025, was $1,551,778 and $ 51,275,253 respectively, representing a decrease in net loss of $49,723,475 or approximately 97%. The decrease in net loss was primarily due to decrease in goodwill impairment of $47,614,729, gain on bankruptcy of subsidiary of 12,019,227 and a decrease in general and administrative expenses of $8,280,982, decrease in the change in fair value of contingent consideration of $10,410,000 and loss on the extinguishment of debt of $7,415,708.

ocf.text: The decrease in our cash used in operating activities is primarily related to the changes in our operating assets and liabilities. The change is primarily driven by our net income offset by significant non-cash charges such as stock-based compensation, impairments and change in fair value of contingent consideration. Additionally, our operating cash flow was positively impacted by changes in our operating assets and liabilities, primarily other receivables, prepaid expenses and accounts payable.

wc.text: Funding that we may receive during the fiscal year 2026 is expected to be used to satisfy existing and future obligations and liabilities and working capital needs, to support commercialization of our products, to conduct the clinical and regulatory work to develop our product candidates, and to begin building working capital reserves.

capex.text: The Company does not have any off-balance sheet arrangements that have or are reasonably likely to have a current or future effect on the Company’s financial condition, changes in financial condition, revenues or expenses, results of operations, liquidity, capital expenditures or capital resources that is material to investors.

net sales.heading: Revenues
net sales.text: We are a pre-clinical biotechnology and artificial intelligence driven healthcare technology company. Our therapeutic and core diagnostic product candidates remain pre-clinical and have not generated any product revenue. During the three and nine months ended March 31, 2026, we recognized $20,942 of service revenue from a single research-services customer (Kapoose Creek Bio Inc.); the Company had no revenues from continuing operations in prior periods. We have incurred losses since inception. We do not anticipate earning material product revenues until our therapies or products are approved for marketing and sale.

opex.heading: Operating Expenses
opex.text:
Our operating expenses for the years ended June 30, 2026 and 2025 were $8,749,925 and $188,966,002, respectively, representing a decrease of $180,216,077 or 95%. The largest contributors to the decrease in operating expenses for the year ended June 30, 2026, were the decreases in the non-cash goodwill impairment of $170,419,429, general and administrative expenses of $10,080,080, and research and development expenses of $512,910, partially offset by the increase in the non-cash long-lived asset impairment of $831,915 compared to the year ended June 30, 2025.

General and administrative expenses for the years ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, were $7,799,970 and $17,880,050, respectively, representing a decrease of $10,080,080, or 56%. The decrease in general and administrative expenses is primarily related to decreases in consulting expenses of $2,137,055, legal expenses of $2,412,596, stock based compensation expense of $2,682,902, salaries of $1,796,534, advertising expenses of $22,899, board member compensation of $29,069, rent expense of $371,441, partially offset by an increase in investor relations expenses of $94,100 and state tax franchise fees of $126,381.

Research and development expenses for the years ended June 30, 2026, and 2025, were $24,518 and $537,428, respectively, representing a decrease of $512,910 or 95%.

The variance is primarily due to a decrease of $11,090,000 in the change in fair value contingent consideration in the current period, loss on extinguishment of debt of 7,415,708 in the current period, which is offset by the gain on bankruptcy of subsidiary in the amount of $12,019,227.

net.heading: Net Loss
net.text: Net loss for the years ended June 30, 2026 and June 30, 2025 was $3,562,479 and $178,007,489, respectively, representing a decrease in net loss of $174,445,010 or 98%. The decrease in net loss was primarily attributable to the absence of the prior-year goodwill impairment of $170,419,429, the $10,080,080 decrease in general and administrative expenses and the $12,019,227 gain on the deconsolidation of GEDi Cube B.V., partially offset by the $7,415,708 loss on extinguishment of debt, the $831,915 impairment of long-lived assets and the $11,090,000 less favorable year-over-year change in the fair value of contingent consideration.

ocf.text: Cash used in operating activities represents the cash receipts and disbursements related to all of our activities other than investing and financing activities. Operating cash flow is derived by adjusting our net loss for non-cash items and changes in operating assets and liabilities. Net cash used in operating activities for the years ended June 30, 2026 and 2025 was $5,288,197 and $7,874,647, respectively, representing a decrease of $2,586,450. The decrease in operating cash usage principally reflects the Company’s lower cash operating cost structure following the restructuring, including reduced payroll and professional-services payments and the elimination of GEDi Cube B.V.’s operating cash requirements after its deconsolidation, together with the timing of payments of liabilities.

intro.text: As of June 30, 2026, Lunai Bioworks Inc. operated principally through two operating subsidiaries, Renovaro Biosciences and BioSymetrics; a third wholly owned subsidiary, Lunai Bioworks IP, Inc., holds the intellectual property acquired in the May 2026 Neurobridge acquisition, including the N2B intranasal drug delivery platform. BioSymetrics refers to BioSymetrics Inc. and its wholly owned subsidiary BioSymetrics Corp., which were acquired on April 8, 2025. During the quarter ended September 30, 2025, GEDi Cube B.V. ("GEDi Cube"), acquired on February 13, 2024, filed for bankruptcy and ceased operations. Following GEDi Cube's bankruptcy and subsequent deconsolidation, the Company continued pursuing its AI-driven precision medicine and biomarker discovery strategy through BioSymetrics, which had been acquired prior to the bankruptcy.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Given these risks and uncertainties, you should not rely on forward-looking statements as a prediction of actual results.

We rely on a combination of patent, copyright, trademark, and trade secret laws, as well as continuing technological innovations, proprietary knowledge, and various third-party agreements, including, without limitation, confidentiality agreements, materials transfer agreements, research agreements, and licensing agreements, to establish and protect our proprietary rights.
Our ability to continue as a going concern will depend on our ability to obtain additional funding, as to which no assurances can be given.
Our future success depends on our ability to raise capital.
Our future capital requirements depend on many factors, including:

Our therapeutic pipeline includes cell, gene and immunotherapy involving genetically modified cells targeted to treat cancer, and we rely on third parties under contract in the development of product candidates in our pipeline.

The commercial success of BioSymetrics’ AI platform and other future products will depend upon the degree of market acceptance by pharmaceutical companies, consumers, including self-insured employers, integrated health systems, healthcare providers.
The degree of market acceptance of these products will depend on a number of factors, including:
BioSymetrics’ success will depend on the market’s confidence that their developed products can provide reliable, high-quality results, once such products are launched.
BioSymetrics relies on third-party collaborators, consultants, contractors, vendors, suppliers and service providers.

The success of our therapeutic research and development efforts will depend upon our ability to demonstrate the efficacy of the treatments in our pipeline in pre-clinical studies, as well as in clinical trials following IND approval by the FDA.

In addition, we expect to rely on clinical trial sites to ensure proper and timely conduct of our future clinical trials and, while we intend to enter into agreements governing their services, we will be limited in our ability to control their actual performance.

We rely upon a combination of patents, trademarks, trade secrets and confidentiality agreements – either that we own or possess or that are owned or possessed by our licensors that are licensed to us – to protect the intellectual property related to our technology and product candidates.

Some of the features in BioSymetrics’ platform are powered by machine learning and AI, which depend on datasets and algorithms that could be flawed, including through inaccurate, insufficient, outdated, or biased data.

Likewise, BioSymetrics relies on third-party research institution collaborators and other third parties to conduct clinical validation, and similar events relating to their computer systems could also have a material adverse effect on BioSymetrics’ business.

BioSymetrics and Renovaro Biosciences rely on trade secrets and confidentiality agreements to protect their know-how, technology, data and other proprietary information and to maintain a competitive position.
We depend on our information technology and telecommunications systems and those of third parties, the failure or disruption of which could harm our business.
In addition, our third-party service providers depend upon technology and telecommunications systems provided by outside vendors.

Renovaro Biosciences’ and BioSymetrics’ success depends on our ability to develop and commercialize our technology without infringing, misappropriating, or otherwise violating the intellectual property of third parties.

Renovaro Biosciences’ and BioSymetrics’ commercial success in part depends upon our ability, and the ability of our collaborators, to market, sell and distribute our products and use our proprietary technologies without infringing, misappropriating or otherwise violating the proprietary rights of third parties.
The success and growth of BioSymetrics’ business depends upon their ability to continuously innovate and develop new products and technologies.
BioSymetrics’ solution is a technology-driven platform that relies on innovation to remain competitive.
We rely on third-party contractors for the provision of professional, scientific, regulatory, and other services.
Because we do not anticipate paying any cash dividends on our capital stock in the foreseeable future, capital appreciation, if any, will be the sole source of potential gain for our stockholders.
As a result, capital appreciation, if any, of our Common Stock will be the sole source of gain for our stockholders for the foreseeable future.

The payment of dividends, if any, is within the discretion of the Board and will depend on the Company’s earnings, if any, its capital requirements and financial condition and such other factors as the Board may consider.
We are currently listed on the Nasdaq Stock Market and therefore rely on the definition of independence set forth in the Nasdaq Listing Rules (“ Nasdaq Rules ”).
